## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components, combined with a fused scatter to the framebuffer, can approach the streaming ceiling.

## Cache saturation
The ns/particle curve is essentially flat across N at every death rate. At q=0.01, cost holds at 24.882–26.561 ns/p from N=10000 through N=10000000, with no knee at the L2 spill (N≈7598, just below the first measured point) or the L3 spill (N≈243148, between N=100000 and N=1000000). The slight rise at N=1000000 (26.561 vs 24.882 at N=100000) is within 7% and recovers at N=10000000 (25.214). Death rate raises the floor monotonically — from ~25 ns/p at q=0.01 to ~33 ns/p at q=0.5 — without altering the N-shape. There is no cache-spill knee because the algo is not memory-bandwidth-limited; the flat curve reflects a compute/frontend bottleneck insensitive to working-set residency.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 2.77 GB/s at N=100000, q=0.01 — only 21.8% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, specifically frontend-bound: the perf profile shows 69–71% frontend stalls, 0% backend stalls, and ~29–31% compute across all N and death rates. Bandwidth never approaches the ceiling at any regime. Rising death rate degrades throughput from 2.77 GB/s (q=0.01) to 2.06 GB/s (q=0.5) as the branchy scatter path fires more often, but the bottleneck class does not change — it stays frontend-bound throughout.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the components of one particle, not across particles. Loop1 loads 16 bytes via `vmovups`, 8 bytes via `vmovsd`, then reshuffles with `vshufps`/`vinsertps` to assemble a 4-float vector, applies `vmulps`/`vaddps`, and writes back with `vmovups`/`vmovlps` — one particle per iteration at stride 0x44 (68 bytes). There is no gather; all loads are sequential from the particle base. Loop2's fused scatter uses byte-granular `movzx`/`add`/`cmp`/`cmovae`/`mov BYTE PTR` sequences per RGBA channel, with extensive branch logic (`sets`, `setge`, `setle`, `jae`, `jne`). The 411-instruction function with this complex control flow explains the 69–71% frontend stalls — the decode front-end cannot sustain throughput, capping bandwidth at 22% of ceiling regardless of cache residency.

## Verdict
Refuted — achieved bandwidth never exceeds 2.77 GB/s (21.8% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate. The compiler did vectorize across components (`vmulps`, `vaddps`), but the one-particle-per-iteration loop with stride-0x44 access and the fused scatter's byte-granular stores with heavy branch logic drive 69–71% frontend stalls. The algo is frontend-bound, not bandwidth-bound, at every measured operating point, so auto-vectorization plus fused scatter cannot approach the streaming ceiling.
